title: Registration data can be linked to an existing identity
description: The flow carries strong identifiers and quasi-identifiers together: email, full name, government ID, and a six-digit code. If the authentication service or connected systems correlate these fields with existing records, the parent can be linked across accounts, sessions, or external datasets.
assumptions: Authentication service stores or can access prior registration, account, or identity records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Parent identity is directly disclosed to the authentication service
description: The registration flow explicitly reveals direct identifiers, including email, name, and government ID, to the authentication service. This creates a privacy threat if collection exceeds what is necessary at this stage or if access is broader than intended.
assumptions: The authentication service receives and processes all listed fields in raw form.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identity disclosure/direct identification.

title: Sensitive registration attributes may be exposed in transit or at intake
description: The flow includes sensitive personal data and credentials: password, government ID, email, name, and a six-digit code. If transport protection, endpoint handling, logging, or input monitoring are inadequate, these attributes could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Threat considers exposure on the data flow and at the receiving process boundary, including logs and monitoring.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data disclosure on a data flow; exact subtree naming may differ.

title: Collection of government ID for registration may enable over-disclosure and profiling
description: Requesting a government ID during parent registration may disclose more personal information than is necessary for basic authentication. This can facilitate broader profiling or unnecessary retention of highly sensitive identity data.
assumptions: Government ID is not strictly required for initial account creation or could be deferred/minimized.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data minimization / excessive disclosure; exact node may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Purpose and consequences of collecting registration fields may be unclear to the parent
description: The parent may not understand why each field is required, especially government ID and the six-digit code, how long the data will be retained, or whether it will be reused for verification, fraud detection, or account recovery. This undermines user awareness.
assumptions: The interface or notice does not clearly explain purpose, retention, sharing, and optionality of each field.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of user awareness/transparency.

title: Registration may process personal data without valid consent or another proper legal basis
description: If the service collects government ID and other personal data during registration without obtaining valid consent where required, or without another appropriate legal basis and clear notice, the processing may be non-compliant with privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy requires consent or another documented legal basis for collecting these fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for consent/non-compliance; legal applicability depends on jurisdiction and system context.

title: Parent may be unable to later deny submission of registration details
description: If the system records the registration submission together with identifying details and verification artifacts, the parent may have limited ability to plausibly deny having submitted the registration data. This can create privacy concerns where deniability is desirable.
assumptions: The service keeps attributable logs or evidence of submission tied to the parent identity.
uncertainty_note: Applicability is context-dependent; non-repudiation is often security-positive, so this is a weaker privacy threat here. Node id is best-fit.

title: Stored parent account record may reveal identity
description: Writing a parent account into the users collection can directly store identifying attributes such as name, email address, phone number, username, or persistent account identifiers. If the datastore is accessed by unauthorized parties or over-broad internal roles, the record can reveal the parent's identity.
assumptions: The parent account record contains direct identifiers or unique account identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for identity disclosure from stored identifying data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Parent account entries may be linkable across services or contexts
description: If the stored parent account uses a stable internal user ID, email address, device-related identifier, or shared foreign keys, records in the users collection may be linked with other datasets or events, enabling correlation of the same parent across contexts.
assumptions: The stored account includes stable identifiers reused elsewhere in the system or analytics pipelines.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Excessive parent profile data in the account record may disclose sensitive information
description: The stored parent account may include more personal data than necessary for authentication, such as full profile details, child relationship metadata, contact preferences, or recovery information. Persisting unnecessary fields increases the amount of personal information exposed if the datastore is queried, misused, or breached.
assumptions: The write operation may include optional or non-essential parent attributes beyond what is strictly needed to maintain the account.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node for disclosure of information through data minimization failure / over-collection in storage.

title: Storing parent account without a defined lawful basis or retention policy may violate privacy expectations
description: If the authentication service stores the parent account in MongoDB without clearly enforcing purpose limitation, retention limits, or consent/contract necessity, the processing may be non-compliant with privacy requirements. This is especially relevant if the account includes family-related data or optional profile attributes.
assumptions: There may be no explicit policy enforcement for lawful basis, purpose limitation, or retention at write time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node for non-compliance related to collection/storage governance; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that parent account details are persisted in the users collection
description: The flow stores a parent account in the backend datastore, but the parent may not be adequately informed about what fields are stored, for what purpose, and for how long. Lack of transparency can undermine user awareness and informed decision-making.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product explanations may be incomplete or not presented at account creation time.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node for insufficient transparency / unawareness; exact node id may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of user attributes in authentication response
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the response includes more personal attributes than necessary for the parent-facing use case, sensitive information about the child account or linked household members may be disclosed to the parent.
assumptions: The 'user data' payload may contain profile, account, or relationship attributes beyond the minimum needed after login.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for attribute disclosure / data minimization issues, but exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: JWT enables cross-context identifiability of the user
description: If the JWT contains stable identifiers, account IDs, email addresses, or other persistent claims, the parent user can identify and correlate the same user across sessions, services, or contexts more easily than necessary.
assumptions: The token or accompanying user data includes persistent identifiers rather than short-lived, context-specific pseudonyms.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability via direct identifiers; exact node id may differ in the official tree.

title: JWT claims allow linkage across services or sessions
description: A JWT often carries stable subject identifiers, tenant IDs, family IDs, or role claims. These can let the recipient link records and actions belonging to the same child or household across multiple interactions, increasing linkability beyond what is necessary for authentication.
assumptions: The JWT is reused across relying parties or contains stable claims that persist over time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability from persistent identifiers in tokens; exact node id may vary.

title: Parent can plausibly deny receipt or use of authentication data
description: If receipt of the JWT and user data is not logged or bound to the parent session, the parent user may later deny having received, viewed, or acted upon the authentication response, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: There is limited audit logging or weak binding between the response and the authenticated parent session.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability depends on whether accountability for receipt/use of this flow is in scope; node id is best effort.

title: Insufficient transparency about JWT contents and downstream use
description: The parent user may not be informed what personal data is embedded in the JWT or included in the returned user data, how long it remains valid, and which downstream components can access it. This reduces user awareness and informed expectations about processing.
assumptions: The system does not clearly explain token contents, retention, recipients, or purposes at the point of authentication.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of information / transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Authentication response may violate data minimization or purpose limitation
description: Returning both a JWT and user data to the parent may exceed what is necessary for the immediate authentication purpose, especially if the payload includes child-related personal data not strictly needed for session establishment. This can create non-compliance with privacy principles or legal obligations.
assumptions: Only a session token or a minimal subset of attributes is necessary for the parent's task.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with privacy principles; exact node id may vary.

title: Authentication service can identify the child via parent email used as login identifier
description: The login flow requires submission of a parent email address together with a password. The authentication service can therefore directly identify or single out the child account through the associated parent email, creating a privacy risk if identity data is processed beyond what is necessary for authentication.
assumptions: Assumes the parent email is stored or otherwise associated with the child account and is visible to or processed by the authentication service as an identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identification may vary.

title: Disclosure of parent email and password in transit or at receipt
description: The flow carries highly sensitive credentials: a parent email address and password. If the transmission channel, endpoint handling, logging, or temporary storage at the authentication service is insufficiently protected, these data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes there is some possibility of interception, insecure endpoint handling, verbose logging, or improper storage of submitted credentials.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact disclosure subtree node may differ depending on whether the focus is transmission, storage, or logging.

title: Login events may be linkable across sessions through reused parent email
description: Because the same parent email is repeatedly used during child login, the authentication service can link multiple login attempts and sessions to the same household or child account. This enables building behavioral patterns over time.
assumptions: Assumes repeated use of the same parent email and retention of authentication logs or session metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact linkability subtree node may vary.

title: User enumeration through login responses may disclose whether a parent email is registered
description: If the authentication service returns different errors or timing behavior for unknown parent emails versus wrong passwords, an attacker may learn whether a given parent email is associated with an account. This discloses account existence and potentially the child's use of the service.
assumptions: Assumes distinguishable authentication responses, timing differences, or recovery prompts based on account existence.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a disclosure/account-enumeration issue and exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of informed submission of parent credentials by the child
description: A child may submit a parent email and password without adequate proof that the parent authorized this use. If the system lacks records of consent or delegated authorization, the parent can later deny having permitted the credential use, creating a privacy and accountability issue around personal data processing.
assumptions: Assumes the service permits child login using parent credentials or parent-linked credentials and does not capture verifiable authorization context.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; mapping to non-repudiation in LINDDUN Pro may vary for consent/authorization evidence scenarios.

title: Processing parent email for child login may exceed data minimization or child-privacy expectations
description: Using a parent's email address as part of a child's login may process personal data that is not strictly necessary or may be incompatible with expectations for child-oriented authentication. Without clear necessity, transparency, and lawful basis, this flow can create non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes applicable child-privacy, consent, or data-minimization obligations and that alternative less intrusive authentication designs may exist.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact non-compliance subtree depends on the regulatory/control objective in scope.

title: Disclosure of child status and profile data to unintended observers on the client side
description: The flow delivers a JWT explicitly indicating userType=child together with child profiles to the Child User endpoint. If the device is shared, compromised, shoulder-surfed, or the response is exposed through browser/app storage, logs, or debugging interfaces, sensitive information about the user being a child and the associated profile data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the child uses a client device or app where tokens/profile data may be visible in memory, storage, UI, logs, or network traces after receipt.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure of message contents; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog wording.

title: Linkability of sessions and activities via persistent JWT identifiers
description: If the JWT contains stable identifiers or claims that persist across sessions, the child's actions across app sessions or services may be linkable. Combining the token with returned child profiles can strengthen correlation between multiple interactions belonging to the same child.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT includes stable subject, profile, or tenant identifiers and is reused across requests or services.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability through persistent identifiers in protocol messages.

title: Inference of minor status from JWT claim userType=child
description: Even if profile fields are minimized, the explicit userType=child claim reveals that the recipient account belongs to a minor. This can expose age-category information and enable sensitive inferences by anyone with access to the token or downstream systems consuming it.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is accessible to client-side code, intermediaries, logs, analytics, or downstream relying parties.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for attribute disclosure/information disclosure by exposed claims; exact subtree naming may differ.

title: Identifiability of the child through profile attributes
description: The child profiles returned in this flow may contain direct or quasi-identifiers such as name, avatar, username, preferences, or unique profile IDs. These attributes can make the child identifiable to parties beyond what is necessary for authentication.
assumptions: Assumes profile payload includes identifiers or combinations of attributes sufficient to single out the child.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from disclosed attributes.

title: Excessive disclosure of child profile data beyond authentication purpose
description: This flow combines authentication material (JWT) with child profiles. Returning profile data in the same response may exceed what is necessary to authenticate the child, conflicting with data minimization and purpose limitation expectations if only an auth token is needed at this stage.
assumptions: Assumes authentication can be completed without sending the full set of child profile attributes in this flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to data minimization/purpose limitation; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Insufficient transparency to the child about JWT claims and profile sharing
description: The child may not understand that authentication returns a token containing role information and that profile data is being transmitted and potentially reused by other components. Lack of clear notice can undermine user awareness and informed expectations about personal-data processing.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not clearly explain token contents, recipients, retention, and uses of child profile data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of transparency/unawareness; exact subtree may vary.

title: Collection of directly identifying child data
description: The flow sends highly identifying attributes for a child profile—name, date of birth, gender, and government ID—to the Child Profile Management process. These attributes can directly identify the child and strongly identify the household relationship when combined.
assumptions: The process stores or otherwise processes the submitted attributes beyond transient transport.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit for identifiability from direct identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node labeling may vary.

title: Linkability of child profile to parent account
description: Because the parent user submits child profile data within an authenticated or attributable interaction, the child identity can be linked to the parent account and potentially to other records about the family across the service.
assumptions: The system can associate this submission with the parent user's account or session.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via account/session association; exact node id may differ in some LINDDUN Pro variants.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child attributes in transit or at intake
description: The flow contains sensitive personal data about a minor, including government ID and date of birth. If the transmission channel, request logging, or intake handling is insufficiently protected, these attributes could be exposed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Transport protection, endpoint hardening, or log minimization may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node selected as a general disclosure/interception-at-transfer best fit; exact subtree placement may vary.

title: Excessive data collection for child profile creation
description: Collecting government ID, full date of birth, and gender at profile-creation time may exceed what is strictly necessary for creating a child profile, creating a risk of unnecessary exposure and retention of a minor's data.
assumptions: Not all listed fields are strictly required for the stated purpose of profile creation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization / unnecessary collection; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency about purpose and use of child data
description: The parent may not be adequately informed why each child attribute is required, how long it will be retained, whether government ID is mandatory, and with whom the data will be shared. This creates a risk that data subjects cannot understand processing implications.
assumptions: The interface or notice at collection may not clearly explain purposes, retention, and sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency at collection; exact node id may vary.

title: Collection of child data without valid legal basis or parental-consent handling
description: Processing a minor's name, DOB, gender, and government ID may require specific legal basis, age-related safeguards, and demonstrable parental authorization. If these are not properly established for this flow, the collection may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable law imposes heightened requirements for children's data and government identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance due to missing legal basis/child-data safeguards; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of parent submission and consent choices
description: If the system does not create reliable records of what child data the parent submitted, when it was submitted, and what notices or consent choices were presented, the parent or operator may later be unable to prove or dispute the submission context.
assumptions: Audit trails or consent receipts may be absent or incomplete for this flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation due to lack of evidence; exact node id may vary.

title: Unauthorized modification of child profile data before storage
description: The child profile management process may update or overwrite profile attributes with incorrect, malicious, or unauthorized values before writing to the childprofiles collection, compromising the integrity of the child's stored profile.
assumptions: P3 accepts profile update inputs from upstream components or users and persists them to DS2.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro integrity subtree labeling may differ.

title: Excessive identifiability of child profiles in storage
description: Stored child profiles may contain direct identifiers or highly specific attributes that make an individual child identifiable within the database, especially when records are retained in clear form or indexed by identifying fields.
assumptions: The childprofiles collection stores personal data such as names, dates of birth, contact details, or unique account identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate for identifiability from stored data.

title: Linkability across profile records and related datasets
description: A persistent child profile record in MongoDB can act as a stable anchor that allows linking the child's data across sessions, services, guardians, educational records, or behavioral datasets, enabling broader profiling than expected.
assumptions: DS2 records use stable identifiers or shared attributes that can be correlated with other collections or systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro linkability subtree may use a more specific child node.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child profile data from the database
description: The childprofiles collection may expose sensitive personal data about children if access controls, encryption, query restrictions, backups, or operational handling are insufficient, leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: DS2 contains personal and possibly sensitive child-related attributes and may be accessible by administrators, services, or backup processes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure from data at rest; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of who changed a child profile
description: If the process does not create reliable audit trails for profile creation and updates, users or administrators may later deny having made a change, and the system may be unable to prove who performed the action and when.
assumptions: Profile updates can be initiated by multiple actors and audit logging may be incomplete or mutable.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact non-repudiation subtree numbering may differ.

title: Unawareness of profile storage or update consequences
description: Children or guardians may be unaware that profile data is being stored, updated, retained, or reused in the childprofiles collection, including what fields are kept and for what downstream purposes.
assumptions: Notice, transparency, or just-in-time explanations about profile persistence may be limited or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness due to insufficient transparency around storage/update operations.

title: Profile storage without adequate legal basis, minimization, or retention controls
description: The process may store or update more child profile data than necessary, retain it longer than justified, or process it without appropriate parental consent, lawful basis, or policy constraints, creating non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The system processes children's personal data subject to heightened legal and policy obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact non-compliance subtree numbering may differ.

title: Search, like, and comment activity can be linked to the same child account or device
description: The service can correlate repeated video searches, requests, likes, and comments from the child user over time, linking actions into a behavioral profile associated with the same account, session, IP address, or device identifiers.
assumptions: The video management service stores identifiers or metadata that allow multiple requests from the same child user to be associated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability of multiple actions within one service; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Child user may be identifiable from account, network, or device metadata
description: Video search and interaction requests may include account identifiers, IP address, cookies, device IDs, or persistent tokens that allow the service to identify the child user directly or indirectly.
assumptions: Requests carry persistent identifiers or are logged with metadata sufficient to single out the child user.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability via direct or indirect identifiers in the flow.

title: Search queries and interactions disclose the child's interests and preferences
description: Search terms, requested videos, likes, and comments can reveal sensitive interests, habits, emotional state, or other personal characteristics of the child to the service operator or anyone with access to logs.
assumptions: The service records content of search queries and interaction payloads.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for exposure of personal content in transmitted or logged requests.

title: Comments may disclose excessive personal information
description: Free-text comments submitted by the child may contain names, contact details, school information, location clues, or other personal data that become visible to the service and potentially others.
assumptions: The flow supports free-text comments and comments are stored or moderated by the service.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree for content-based disclosure from user-generated text may differ; node id is approximate.

title: The child may be unaware that searches, likes, and comments are logged and profiled
description: The service may process and retain interaction data for recommendation, moderation, analytics, or advertising purposes without the child clearly understanding that these actions are observed, stored, and analyzed.
assumptions: Notices are absent, unclear, or not understandable to children.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness node for insufficient user awareness of observation and logging.

title: Secondary use of interaction data may be unclear to the child
description: Data from searches, requests, likes, and comments may be reused for personalization, analytics, safety monitoring, or marketing-related purposes beyond what the child expects, without meaningful understanding or control.
assumptions: The service uses interaction data for purposes beyond immediate content retrieval and display.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node for unclear purposes and downstream processing; exact node id may vary.

title: Processing of a child's interaction data may occur without valid consent or other lawful basis
description: Because the flow involves a child user's searches, likes, comments, and viewing requests, the service may process personal data without age-appropriate consent, parental authorization where required, or another valid legal basis.
assumptions: The child is below the applicable age threshold and the jurisdiction requires consent, parental authorization, or special protections for children's data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for lack of lawful basis/children's privacy obligations; exact node id is approximate.

title: Data minimization and purpose-limitation obligations may be violated
description: Collecting full search histories, detailed engagement events, and comment content for longer than necessary or for unrelated purposes may exceed what is needed to provide the video service, especially for a child user.
assumptions: The service retains detailed logs or uses them beyond the immediate service purpose.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for non-compliance with minimization, retention, or purpose-limitation requirements.

title: The child may later be unable to deny having submitted a like or comment
description: If the service binds likes or comments to the child's account, device, or session and keeps logs, those records can be used as evidence that the child performed the action, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: The service stores attributable logs of user interactions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation due to attributable logging of actions.

title: Excessive video metadata stored enables identification of individuals
description: When the Video Management Service stores video metadata in MongoDB, fields such as uploader account identifiers, device identifiers, IP addresses, timestamps, geolocation, or embedded EXIF-like attributes can directly or indirectly identify a person associated with a video.
assumptions: The metadata schema may include account, device, network, or location-related attributes beyond what is strictly necessary for core video management.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for storing directly/indirectly identifying data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Linkability across videos through persistent identifiers in metadata
description: Persistent uploader IDs, channel IDs, device IDs, or stable storage keys written with each video record can allow multiple videos and related actions to be linked to the same individual or household over time.
assumptions: The service stores stable identifiers with each video record and these are accessible for analytics, administration, or downstream processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers.

title: Sensitive attributes disclosed through stored video metadata
description: Metadata stored in the collection may reveal personal information such as location, recording time patterns, social relationships, behavioral habits, or special-category data inferred from titles, tags, descriptions, thumbnails, or moderation labels.
assumptions: Video metadata includes user-supplied or system-generated descriptive fields that may contain sensitive content or enable inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of personal/sensitive data in stored content.

title: Unauthorized retrieval of video metadata from datastore
description: If access controls, query restrictions, or encryption protections on MongoDB are insufficient, unauthorized parties or over-privileged internal components may retrieve stored video metadata and associated references to files.
assumptions: The datastore may be queried by multiple services or administrators, and not all accesses are equally constrained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unauthorized access/disclosure from a datastore; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that metadata and file references are persistently stored
description: The flow stores and retrieves video metadata and file references in a backend datastore, but users may not understand the extent, duration, or granularity of retained metadata, including derived attributes generated during processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or UI cues may not clearly explain backend persistence of metadata and associated files.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency about collection and storage.

title: Storage of unnecessary metadata or retention beyond stated purpose
description: The service may write more metadata than needed for video management, or retain metadata and file references longer than necessary, creating purpose-limitation and data-minimization compliance risks.
assumptions: No strict schema minimization or retention enforcement is applied before writing to MongoDB.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with minimization/retention obligations.

title: Insufficient auditability of metadata writes and reads
description: If writes, updates, and retrievals of video metadata in MongoDB are not logged with adequate integrity and attribution, the service or operators may later be unable to prove what personal data was stored or accessed, undermining accountability and enabling repudiation.
assumptions: Audit logging for datastore operations may be incomplete, mutable, or not tied to authenticated actors.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation due to inadequate logging/accountability.

title: Inference of personal behavior from aggregated video records
description: Even if individual metadata fields seem harmless, storing many video records together enables profiling of upload habits, activity times, interests, locations, and relationships through aggregation and analysis.
assumptions: Multiple records per user are retained and can be queried or analyzed together.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure via inference/profiling from aggregated stored data.

title: Linkability of a child's activities across sessions
description: Storing search and watch history in a persistent child profile allows records from different sessions and times to be linked to the same child account or profile, enabling reconstruction of behavior patterns and interests over time.
assumptions: The history entries are stored with a stable child/profile identifier or otherwise remain associated to the same profile over time.

description: The stored search and watch history can reveal sensitive personal data about a child, such as health concerns, emotional state, religion, sexuality-related curiosity, or other intimate interests, if accessed beyond the intended purpose.

title: Unawareness of history storage and profiling

assumptions: The system may not provide clear, age-appropriate notice or parental transparency about this storage and use.

title: Excessive retention or purpose-incompatible storage of child activity history
description: Persistently storing child search and watch history may violate data minimization, storage limitation, or purpose limitation expectations if more data is kept than necessary, retained too long, or reused for secondary purposes.
assumptions: There may be no strict retention limit, minimization, or narrowly defined purpose for the stored history.

assumptions: No effective user-facing controls or backend support exist for access, rectification, or erasure of history records.

assumptions: The video contains rich visual/audio context and is reviewed or processed by the service for approval decisions.

title: Identifiability of parent or child from video content and metadata
description: Faces, voices, names spoken in audio, school uniforms, home interiors, EXIF/device metadata, or other contextual clues in the uploaded video may directly identify the parent, child, or household members.
assumptions: Uploaded videos may include biometric or contextual identifiers and metadata is not fully stripped before processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; selected as a generic identifiability node.

title: Insufficient awareness of approval/rejection criteria and video handling
description: The parent may not be adequately informed about what parts of the video are reviewed, whether automated analysis is used, how approval/rejection is determined, how long the video is retained, or who can access it. This creates a detectability/disclosure concern around opaque processing of submitted content.
assumptions: Notices may be incomplete or not presented at upload time.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN Pro node choice is uncertain here because disclosure-of-information and detectability subtrees can be modeled differently across versions.

title: Unawareness of secondary use of uploaded videos
description: Parents may be unaware that uploaded videos could be reused for staff training, model improvement, abuse detection tuning, analytics, or policy enforcement beyond the immediate approval/rejection purpose.
assumptions: The service may reserve broad reuse rights or describe them unclearly in privacy notices.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; selected as a generic unawareness node.

title: Processing of video beyond necessity or without valid consent/appropriate legal basis
description: Collecting and processing full video uploads for approval/rejection may exceed data minimization expectations if less intrusive evidence would suffice, and may involve children’s data or special-category data requiring stronger safeguards, consent handling, or other legal basis controls.
assumptions: The flow may involve minors and rich media containing more personal data than strictly necessary for the decision.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id is approximate; using a generic non-compliance node because exact legal-basis/minimization subtree ids vary.

title: Parent cannot later prove what video was submitted or what decision was communicated
description: If the service does not provide reliable receipts, timestamps, hashes, or decision records, the parent may be unable to demonstrate which video was uploaded, when it was submitted, and whether it was approved or rejected. This can undermine accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: The system may lack user-visible submission receipts or immutable audit trails.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; selected as a generic non-repudiation threat node.

title: Exposure of child's viewing choice to unintended recipients during streaming
description: If the approved video stream or associated metadata is delivered over an insecure or improperly scoped channel, network observers or other unauthorized parties could learn which video the child is watching, revealing preferences or behavioral information.
assumptions: The stream may traverse networks or intermediaries where confidentiality controls could be weak or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether content, metadata, or communication confidentiality is modeled separately.

title: Child can be observed as recipient of specific streamed content
description: The act of receiving a particular approved video can disclose the child's interests, habits, or profile to parties able to observe the delivery endpoint, session identifiers, or playback events.
assumptions: An observer can correlate the child user's endpoint or account with the streamed video session.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a detectability/inference risk from observing delivery to the child.

title: Stream delivery identifiers enable linking of multiple viewing sessions
description: Persistent account identifiers, device identifiers, cookies, or stable stream tokens used by the video management service could allow multiple viewing sessions to be linked together, building a profile of the child over time.
assumptions: The service uses stable identifiers across sessions or across videos.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact subtree for linkability via persistent identifiers may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Child may be identifiable through stream metadata or identifiers
description: Even if the video content is approved, metadata in the stream delivery such as account name, user ID, device ID, or personalized URLs may directly or indirectly identify the child to intermediaries or third parties.
assumptions: Identifiers are exposed in requests, headers, URLs, logs, or CDN interactions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; identifiability may be represented under a more specific metadata/identifier branch.

title: Streaming beyond the approved purpose or consent scope
description: The service may use the streaming interaction and playback telemetry for purposes beyond delivering the approved video to the child, such as profiling, recommendations, analytics, or sharing with third parties, without valid consent or another lawful basis.
assumptions: Playback events or delivery metadata are collected and reused beyond strict service delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact non-compliance branch depends on the modeled legal/privacy requirement.

title: Insufficient evidence of what was streamed to the child and under what approval
description: If the service lacks trustworthy records of which approved video was streamed, when, and under which authorization context, it may be impossible to later demonstrate compliance with parental approval decisions or investigate disputes.
assumptions: Audit logging or integrity protection for approval and delivery events is incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; repudiation threats are less commonly emphasized for this simple delivery flow but can apply where accountability is required.

title: Excessive playback telemetry discloses sensitive behavioral details
description: Fine-grained telemetry generated while streaming to the child, such as timestamps, pauses, rewinds, completion rates, and device/network details, can disclose sensitive behavioral patterns beyond what is necessary to deliver the video.
assumptions: The service or downstream processors collect detailed playback and device telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact disclosure subtree may distinguish content disclosure from metadata/behavioral disclosure.

title: Linkability of child activity records across sessions and contexts
description: Browsing data stored in the childprofiles collection and sent to the AI Recommendation Engine may allow the engine to correlate records belonging to the same child across sessions, devices, or service contexts, enabling construction of a persistent behavioral profile.
assumptions: The browsing data includes stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers such as account ID, device ID, cookie, IP history, or consistent behavioral features.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering for linkability of data records may vary by catalog edition.

title: Identifiability of a child from browsing data used by the AI engine
description: Even if direct identifiers are minimized, the transferred browsing history may contain unique combinations of pages viewed, timestamps, interests, or metadata that allow the AI engine or connected components to identify a specific child.
assumptions: The AI engine has access to auxiliary data, account context, or sufficiently granular browsing events.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from data content.

title: Inference of sensitive child attributes from browsing behavior
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may infer sensitive information about a child, such as health concerns, emotional state, religion, sexuality, vulnerabilities, or special educational needs, from browsing patterns beyond what was originally collected.
assumptions: The recommendation model performs profiling or feature extraction on detailed browsing data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure-related node id is uncertain; threat clearly concerns inference/disclosure from observed behavior.

title: Excessive disclosure of child browsing data to the AI engine
description: The full child browsing dataset may be disclosed from the datastore to the AI engine even when only a subset or aggregated features are necessary for recommendations, increasing exposure of personal data.
assumptions: Data minimization controls are not yet defined for this planned flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unnecessary data disclosure; numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Secondary use of child browsing data for model training or analytics
description: Browsing data sent for generating recommendations may also be used to train models, evaluate engagement, or develop new features without the child or guardian reasonably understanding this additional purpose.
assumptions: The planned AI pipeline may retain inputs for training, tuning, monitoring, or experimentation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness regarding secondary processing purposes; exact numbering may vary.

title: Processing child browsing data without a valid lawful basis or age-appropriate safeguards
description: Sending child browsing data from the childprofiles collection to an AI Recommendation Engine may be incompatible with consent obtained, exceed parental expectations, or violate child-specific legal requirements if appropriate lawful basis, transparency, and safeguards are absent.
assumptions: This is a planned flow and compliance controls, parental consent handling, and child-specific governance may not yet be finalized.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id; exact mapping depends on the LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The planned flow sends users' browsing data from the AI Recommendation Engine to external advertisers. Browsing histories and interaction patterns can reveal interests, habits, and potentially sensitive inferences, exposing personal data to parties outside the primary service context.
assumptions: Browsing data contains user-level or pseudonymous identifiers, behavioral events, or attributes linkable to an individual or household.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether the data is directly identifiable or pseudonymous.

title: Linkability of user activity across contexts
description: Third-party advertisers receiving browsing data may link records from this service with data from other publishers, ad-tech partners, or existing profiles, enabling cross-context correlation of the same user or device.
assumptions: Advertisers possess additional identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, or partner datasets that can be matched with the received browsing data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via correlating datasets.

title: Identifiability of users from browsing data
description: Even if the shared browsing data is intended to be pseudonymous, advertisers may be able to identify specific individuals by combining behavioral patterns, identifiers, location/time signals, or existing customer data.
assumptions: The flow includes persistent identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or sufficiently granular event data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; identifiability may depend on exact fields shared and advertiser-side enrichment capabilities.

title: Unawareness of advertising data sharing
description: Users may be unaware that their browsing data is being shared with third-party advertisers for advertising or profiling purposes, especially if this is only planned, not clearly disclosed, or buried in notices.
assumptions: Privacy notices, consent prompts, or just-in-time disclosures are absent, unclear, or incomplete regarding this specific sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of user awareness/transparency.

title: Secondary use of browsing data for profiling and ad targeting
description: Advertisers may use the received browsing data for purposes beyond the user's reasonable expectations, such as profile enrichment, audience segmentation, retargeting, lookalike modeling, or onward sharing within ad-tech ecosystems.
assumptions: Contractual and technical controls do not strictly limit purpose and downstream use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for use of data beyond the original or expected purpose.

title: Potential non-compliance due to sharing browsing data with third parties
description: Sending browsing data to advertisers may violate privacy requirements if there is no valid legal basis, inadequate consent for advertising cookies/profiling, insufficient transparency, or missing data-sharing agreements and transfer safeguards.
assumptions: Applicable laws or internal policies require explicit notice, consent, purpose limitation, minimization, and vendor/transfer controls for this type of sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction, data categories, and implementation details.

title: Insufficient accountability for advertiser receipt and use
description: After disclosure to third-party advertisers, it may be difficult to prove what data was received, how it was used, whether it was further shared, or whether deletion/objection requests were honored, reducing accountability and auditability.
assumptions: Logging, contractual audit rights, and downstream usage reporting are limited or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of provability/accountability in third-party processing.

title: Stored government ID images reveal highly sensitive personal data if accessed by unauthorized parties
description: Government ID images stored in the backend file system may contain names, photos, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, and document metadata. If file permissions, storage isolation, or access controls are weak, unauthorized internal users, compromised services, or attackers could access the images and learn sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The file system is reachable by multiple services or administrators, or stored files are not strongly access-controlled and encrypted.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure from data at rest; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Government ID images can be linked to user accounts or other records
description: Persisting ID images in a backend uploads directory creates a durable identifier-rich artifact that can be linked with authentication records, account profiles, device logs, or case-management data. This enables correlation of a person's identity across contexts beyond the immediate verification purpose.
assumptions: The stored files are named, indexed, or referenced in a way that associates them with account identifiers, sessions, or other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability/linkability via stored identifiers; exact subtree naming may differ.

title: Stored ID images may enable linking of the same individual across transactions or systems
description: Because government ID images are unique and persistent, storing them in the file system can allow the same person to be recognized and linked across multiple uploads, verification attempts, tenants, or downstream systems, especially if filenames, hashes, or extracted document attributes are reused.
assumptions: The system retains images or derived identifiers long enough to compare across events or shares them with other components.
uncertainty_note: Potential overlap with Identifiability depending on taxonomy boundaries; node id is best-effort.

title: Retention of government ID images in uploads storage may exceed necessity or legal basis
description: Storing raw government ID images in backend/uploads/ may violate data minimization, storage limitation, or purpose limitation obligations if the images are kept longer than needed for authentication or retained without a clear lawful basis, notice, or deletion policy.
assumptions: The system stores full images rather than ephemeral processing outputs and may lack strict retention/deletion enforcement.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node for excessive retention/purpose limitation; exact node id may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient evidence of consent or submission context for stored ID images
description: If the authentication service stores government ID images without recording the user's submission context, consent, notice version, or verification purpose, the organization may later be unable to demonstrate that collection and storage were authorized and properly communicated, enabling repudiation by the data subject or operator.
assumptions: The flow stores the image itself but may not reliably bind it to auditable records of notice, consent, or transaction context.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less direct on this storage flow than disclosure/non-compliance; included because auditable proof of collection purpose may be missing.

title: Users may be unaware that raw government ID images are stored in backend uploads storage
description: The storage operation may be opaque to users, who might believe their ID is only transiently checked rather than retained as a file. Lack of transparency about storage location, duration, access, and downstream use undermines users' ability to understand privacy consequences.
assumptions: Privacy notices or UI do not clearly explain that raw ID images are retained after upload for authentication purposes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness node for insufficient transparency; exact node id may vary.

title: JWT in localStorage can reveal user identity or account attributes
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage exposes token contents to any script running in the origin and to anyone with access to the browser profile. If the JWT contains subject identifiers, roles, email address, tenant identifiers, or other claims, those claims can disclose the user's identity or personal attributes.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted and contains readable claims, as is common for bearer JWTs.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure of stored data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Persistent JWT enables cross-session linkability
description: A JWT persisted in localStorage can act as a stable pseudonymous identifier across browser sessions. Scripts or components within the same origin can use the token or its claims to correlate repeated visits and actions to the same user over time.
assumptions: Assumes the token lifetime or refresh pattern makes it stable enough to correlate sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifier in client-side storage; exact node id may differ.

title: JWT storage in localStorage increases detectability of logged-in state
description: The presence of a JWT in localStorage makes it easy for scripts executing in the origin to detect whether a user is authenticated, even without using the token. This reveals the existence of a user account or active session on the service.
assumptions: Assumes same-origin scripts or browser extensions can inspect localStorage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability of a subject's presence/state from stored authentication artifacts; exact node id may differ.

title: LocalStorage token persistence may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Persisting authentication tokens in localStorage can retain personal data on the device longer than users expect, especially across browser restarts or shared-device use. If users are not clearly informed or given meaningful control, this can conflict with data minimization, storage limitation, or consent/expectation requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the service does not clearly disclose this storage behavior or provide adequate controls such as logout clearing and session-only storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance related to excessive retention/transparency around client-side storage; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that authentication data is stored persistently on the device
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage is typically invisible to end users. Users may not understand that authentication data remains on the device after closing the browser, which can undermine informed decision-making about using shared or unmanaged devices.
assumptions: Assumes no prominent notice or UI indication is provided about persistent local storage of authentication data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Exposure of child history to an unintended parent or guardian
description: If Child Profile Management returns child history to the wrong parent account, or if authorization checks are weak or bypassed, sensitive child history may be disclosed to an unauthorized recipient.
assumptions: The flow contains potentially sensitive child-related historical data and relies on application-layer access control to ensure only the correct parent can review it.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized disclosure of data in transit/application response; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Parent can link child history across contexts or services
description: The returned child history may contain stable identifiers, timestamps, or rich event details that allow the parent or anyone viewing the response to link the child's activities across different contexts, periods, or related services beyond what is necessary for review.
assumptions: The history payload includes identifiers or detailed records spanning multiple events or systems.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via identifiers/metadata in disclosed records.

title: Overly detailed child history enables profiling of the child
description: Providing a full or highly granular history to the parent may reveal patterns about the child's behavior, health, learning, location, or habits, enabling inference of sensitive attributes beyond the immediate review purpose.
assumptions: History records are sufficiently detailed or longitudinal to support inference of sensitive traits or patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/discoverability through inference from detailed records; exact node may differ in your LINDDUN Pro taxonomy.

title: Parent can deny having viewed sensitive child history
description: If the system does not create reliable, privacy-respecting audit evidence of access, a parent may later repudiate having reviewed the child's history, undermining accountability for sensitive data access.
assumptions: Access logging or acknowledgment of review may be absent, incomplete, or not integrity-protected.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation of data access; exact node naming may vary.

title: Child history shared beyond consented or expected purpose
description: Returning child history to the parent for review may exceed the child's, guardian's, or regulatory consent boundaries if the data includes categories, time ranges, or sources not covered by the original notice or lawful basis.
assumptions: Consent, notice, or legal basis may be scoped narrowly, and the response could include data outside that scope.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance with consent/purpose limitation; exact node id may vary.

title: Parent is unaware of the extent and sensitivity of returned child history
description: The interface or response may not clearly communicate what child history is being shown, why it is available, how current it is, or how it may be used, limiting the parent's and child's awareness and ability to exercise privacy choices.
assumptions: Transparency notices or contextual explanations are limited or absent in the review flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient transparency/unawareness; exact node naming may vary.
